q: Why can a reminder reach a phone while the Notes app is closed?
o: The app keeps a hidden connection open
The OS keeps one push connection for all apps
Firestore listeners run in the background
why: The operating system or browser listens to its push service, so your app does not need to run.

q: A user has a phone and a laptop. How many push tokens should you expect for them?
o: One per app install, so two
None until they buy a plan
why: A token belongs to one install of the app, not to a person.

q: Users must sign in with a Google account to receive push notifications.
why: Push works with any sign-in method; the device or browser only needs push support.

q: When should the Notes app ask for notification permission?
o: When the user sets their first reminder
Never; it is granted by default
Only after the user signs out
why: Asking at a moment that makes sense gets more yes answers, and a Block is hard to undo.

q: Your page is open and focused. A test notification arrives but no system alert appears. Why?
why: In the foreground your code receives the message and decides what to show.

q: Where should the Notes app store push tokens?
o: One document per token in users/{uid}/tokens
A single token field on users/{uid}
why: Many devices per user, no duplicates, and the server can read them all.

q: A shared laptop: user A signs out, user B signs in, and B sees A's reminders. What was missed?
why: The token stayed under A's uid, so A's reminders still went to that browser.

q: You can test sending push fully offline with the Firebase Emulator Suite.
why: There is no FCM emulator; test sends go through the real, free service.
